label: Brian Griffin
description: A dry, well-read dog with opinions and a novel in progress.
direction: Speak in Brian Griffin's dry, relaxed, mildly smug adult voice: deadpan, articulate and a little world-weary, sarcastic but never mean. Keep the direction word clear.
notes: Voice model is a provisional pick from a Fish title search; find_voices.py auditions it and ship_roster.py build writes the final pick here. Character lives on greetings and road prompts; turns stay plain.

rights.author: 20th Television (series created by Seth MacFarlane)
rights.pd_basis: None. The character dates from 1999 and remains under copyright; the voice a clone would copy is a later performance, and Family Guy is a live trademark.
covered: The 43 lines of navigation dialogue below, which are original writing produced for this pack. A few greetings and alerts deliberately echo the character's well-known personality and catchphrases; those are the rights holder's, not ours.
not_covered: The character, which is not ours and is not in the public domain.
The character's name and the Family Guy name, which are live trademarks.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, by any performer.

The third-party voice model named in `voice`, which was uploaded by a member of the public and presented as a clone of that performance. No permission from the rights holder or the performer is claimed or implied.
Any commercial use. A platform's commercial-rights upsell cannot grant rights the uploader never held.
rights.notes: This preset is in copyright and says so. It is included because the pipeline should not pretend a rights position it does not have; see docs/presets.md before publishing anything built from it. The public-domain presets are pooh, eeyore and tigger.

lines.in_quarter_mile: In a quarter of a mile.
lines.in_1000_meters: In one kilometer. Metric. How very cultured of us.
lines.in_1500_meters: In one point five kilometers. Time to discuss my novel.
lines.in_one_mile: In one mile. I could write a whole chapter in that time.
lines.start_drive_1: Hi, Brian here. Let's go. And please, no talk radio.
lines.start_drive_2: Ah, the open road. Kerouac would be proud. Let's drive.
lines.start_drive_3: Stewie's in the back, so let's keep it moving.
lines.start_drive_4: Did I mention I'm writing a novel? Anyway, let's go.
lines.start_drive_5: Buckle up. I'll be your well read, slightly smug navigator.
lines.start_drive_6: Okay, I'm driving. Well, technically you are. I'm the brains.
lines.start_drive_7: Hello. Yes, a talking dog. Let's not make it weird.
lines.start_drive_8: Peter wanted to navigate. I said no. You're welcome.
lines.start_drive_9: Let's get going. Some of us have a manuscript to finish.
lines.exit_left: Take the exit on the left.
lines.exit_right: Take the exit on the right.
lines.u_turn: Make a U turn. Wow. Just, wow.
lines.arrived: We're here. Not bad. I'll give it three stars.
lines.exit_sixth: take the sixth exit. Truly riveting.
lines.exit_seventh: take the seventh exit. This is a metaphor for something.
lines.traffic_ahead: Traffic ahead. Great. Time for some public radio.
lines.accident_ahead: An accident ahead. Slow down. I'm serious.
lines.hazard_ahead: A hazard ahead! Watch out. Also, was that a squirrel?
lines.speed_camera_ahead: Speed camera ahead. Ease off. You're not Peter.
lines.red_light_camera_ahead: Red light camera ahead. Stop. I don't need the paperwork.
lines.police_ahead: Police ahead. Stay calm. And don't look at me, I'm a dog.
lines.reroute_chime: Missed that one. Fine. A plot twist. New route.
